subject: Request: weighted SLO epoch and transient carveouts for Hosted API (p50/p95)
messages:
From: Scott Evans <scott.evans@finapp.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Hosted API latency - request for temporary measurement adjustment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're ramping a new realtime orchestration flow and seeing predictable daytime spikes (09:00-18:00 PT) that push our p95 above the current contract band during business hours even though p50 is well within target. This is durable — not noise — and it's causing customer-facing throttles.

Two asks:
- Would Redwood consider a temporary, daypart-aware measurement approach (daytime weight > nighttime) or a weighted epoch instead of straight rolling-day percentiles?
- If not, can we get an exception carveout for predictable scheduled bursts (campaigns) with strict telemetry and a 60–90 day horizon?

We're trying to avoid a contract amendment if possible — prefer an ops-level carveout and can provide traffic traces and a lightweight canary test window. We're aiming for: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 900ms (with daytime-weighted accounting) for the next 90 days.

Happy to jump on a quick call.

—Scott
Scott Evans
Director, Platform Engineering | FinApp
scott.evans@finapp.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: finapp-latency-evidence-202604.csv (CSV of sample traces)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Scott Evans <scott.evans@finapp.com>
Cc: k***@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency - request for temporary measurement adjustment

Scott — thanks for the data and context. We can be pragmatic here: Redwood is open to a timeboxed, evidence-backed carveout that uses a weighted epoch calculation instead of a simple rolling percentile for the duration of the recovery window. A few high-level points:

- Proposal (ops carveout, 90-day max): define a weighted 30-day epoch where daytime samples (09:00-18:00 PT) count 2x, nighttime 1x. Compute p50/p95 over the weighted sample set.
- Baseline targets (to be agreed): p50 <= 120ms; p95 <= 900ms (same numeric targets you suggested).
- Constraints: carveout only applies when FinApp signals a scheduled campaign (via Ops tag) or when observed traffic matches the provided trace signature. We'll require SDK telemetry tags and a short evidence packet weekly.
- Fallbacks: if weighted epoch shows degradation beyond agreed thresholds for 14 consecutive days, Redwood will apply automatic throttling and notify account team.

I'll draft a short ops addendum (not a full contract amendment) and run this past our SRE and Legal. Can you confirm you can instrument the SDK tag and share a 7-day canary window starting the week of May 11?

Next steps: if you agree we will: 1) deliver a one-page addendum, 2) schedule a 30-min runbook sync, 3) start a 7-day canary.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachment: slo-proposal-weighted-epoch-v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API latency - request for temporary measurement adjustment

Soojin — quick tech read from SRE:

On the weighted epoch idea: doable but we should be explicit about sampling bias and production observability. My notes:
- Implementation: apply sample weighting at aggregation time in our measurement pipeline (no model changes).
- Canary: recommend a 7-day canary against a small subset of traffic with both weighted and unweighted metrics reported; keep raw traces for audit.
- Limits: prefer 90-day max, but add an automatic 14-day rollback if p95 persists above 1.25x target after canary.
- Cost/ops: increased dashboarding and weekly evidence review; likely support time from Solutions for the first 30 days (~8-12 engineer-hours).

Also propose adding an automatic policy to route heavy daytime requests to a lower-cost quantized variant if latency climbs past emergency thresholds; that reduces cost impact and preserves availability.

If Legal wants template language I'll collaborate with Marissa.

—Karthik
Sr. SRE Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Scott Evans <scott.evans@finapp.com>
Cc: k***@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency - request for temporary measurement adjustment

Scott — attaching the short ops addendum (PDF) with the weighted-epoch definition and acceptance criteria. Key changes from my earlier note:
- Weighted epoch: 30-day window, daytime (09:00-18:00 PT) samples weight=3, nighttime weight=1 (we increased the day weight to be conservative to match your usage profile).
- Maximum term: 90 days from go-live; automatic audit at day 30 and day 60.
- Telemetry requirements: SDK tag "finapp_campaign=1" + export of the weekly evidence CSV.
- Emergency fallback: route to quantized-variant-q4 if p95 > 1.25x agreed threshold for 12 hours; notify account/CS.

Can you confirm: 1) FinApp can add the SDK tag, 2) you approve the weight=3 daytime multiplier, and 3) whether you want the canary to start week of May 11 or May 18.

Once you confirm I'll have Legal prepare the brief addendum and Finance draft an MPA-style acceptance that doesn't touch unit price.

Best,
Soojin
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: slo-proposal-weighted-epoch-v1.pdf

From: Scott Evans <scott.evans@finapp.com>

Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700

Soojin — thanks, the proposal looks good and the weight=3 daytime multiplier is acceptable. We can instrument the SDK tag this week and are happy to run the 7-day canary starting May 11.

Couple quick clarifications:
- For the quantized fallback: will responses be deterministic parity-wise? Our product team is okay with slightly reduced throughput quality but needs to understand any semantic divergence risk.
- Please send the addendum and DocuSign link so I can get our procurement to sign off.

I'll upload a small sample dataset to the drive link and we will enable the SDK tag by May 7. Looking forward to the canary.

—Scott
Director, Platform Engineering | FinApp
